# Things to do in Pembrokeshire

Discover some of the many great things to do in Pembrokeshire. It's a magnet for walkers, nature lovers, foodies and families. There are so many amazing places to visit in Pembrokeshire, including Victorian seaside towns and intimate coves.

SaveShare

## Beautiful beaches

With so many beautiful beaches, the seaside is one of the many places to visit in Pembrokeshire for a great time.

### Tenby

A Victorian seaside town with picture-postcard qualities, the rise of [Dinbych-y-Pysgod](https://www.visitwales.com/node/2938) (Tenby) came with ringing medical endorsements for its health-giving properties. It remains a major attraction for young and old. [Castle Beach](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1443775) was even awarded ‘Britain’s Best Beach 2019’ by the Sunday Times.

The [monastery on Caldey Island](https://www.visitwales.com/product/2174030), just a short boat ride from Dinbych-y-Pysgod, is also well worth a visit.

### Freshwater West

What makes your perfect day out at the beach? Plenty of space to run about, rockpools to discover mysterious sea creatures, sandcastle building heaven? With it's wide, sandy beach, [Freshwater West](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1936408) ticks all the boxes.

Plus, if you're looking for some action on the waves, it's also popular with experienced surfers due to the strong currents. If it all seems a bit familiar, the beach has also starred in _Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows_ – Shell Cottage was built here as the home of Bill Weasley and Fleur Delacour.

Freshwater West is a dog-friendly beach. Read more about [dog-friendly Pembrokeshire: perfect for adventures on land and sea](https://www.visitwales.com/node/5543).

## Unbeatable walks

With miles of coast, hills and plenty of places to enjoy nature, there are some fantastic walks in Pembrokeshire.

### Pembrokeshire Coast National Park

[Pembrokeshire Coast National Park](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3823) is the only national park in the UK to be focused primarily along dramatic coastline. Yes it's a feast for the eyes, abundant in wildlife and rare flora and fauna, but it also has numerous monuments and sites of historic interest. There's never a dull moment here.

Read more: [Things to see and do on the Pembrokeshire Coast Path](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3152)

### The Preseli Hills

Clear days in the [Preseli Hills](http://www.visitpembrokeshire.com/explore-pembrokeshire/preseli-mountains/) offer views as far as the Wicklow Mountains in Ireland. Stones from the area are believed to have been transported 180 miles to Stonehenge and new research also suggests that people from West Wales may have helped in its construction. Numerous Neolithic burial chambers, stone circles and Iron Age forts offer an intriguing insight to the great history of these hills. Follow the ancient [Golden Road](https://www.visitpembrokeshire.com/articles/walking-on-the-golden-road) high in the hills to see them for yourself.

While you're there, step back in time with a visit to [Tafarn Sinc](https://www.tafarnsinc.cymru/), the highest licensed pub in Pembrokeshire. The pub has a fascinating history and continues to uphold traditions of the area to this day. And their Sunday lunch is pretty good too!

![Bedd Arthur or Arthur's Grave which is a possible Neolithic hengiform monument megalithic site in the Preseli Hills](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__landscape__2_1x/public/media-library/2020-08/SVW-C27-1718-0033.jpg.webp?itok=9vlAVI-p)

## Activities, attractions and events

If you're looking for what to do in Pembrokeshire, you won't be disappointed. There are many [activities](https://www.visitwales.com/search?search=Pembrokeshire&location=&lat=51.67624559999999&long=-4.918369999999999&radius=80450&unit=miles&sliderValue=5&sector%5B0%5D=Activity) to enjoy in this beautiful part of Wales. There's a good range of [Pembrokeshire attractions](https://www.visitwales.com/search?search=Pembrokeshire&location=&lat=51.67624559999999&long=-4.918369999999999&radius=80450&unit=miles&sliderValue=5&sector%5B0%5D=Attraction) too. Here are some of the highlights.

### Stackpole Nature Reserve

[Stackpole Nature Reserve](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1867015) is a beautiful stretch of coastline offering varied attractions including stunning beaches like [Barafundle Bay](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1443789), contrasting with the picturesque [Bosherston Lakes](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/stackpole/features/bosherston-lakes-and-stackpole-court) near Stackpole Court. There are many activities including kayaking and coasteering, as well as plenty of delicious local produce to sample in the tea rooms.

### St Davids Cathedral

With a population of less than 2,000, Tyddewi (St Davids) is more than a record-holder as Britain's smallest city. [St Davids Cathedral](https://www.visitwales.com/product/509444) is a magnificent cathedral that has been a place of pilgrimage since the 12th century and there are several other attractions of artistic and culinary kinds.

### Coasteering

According to those in the know, [coasteering](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3255) was first practiced along the coast of Pembrokeshire, the craggy rocks providing the perfect playground for leaping into the clean blue waters. It's great fun too, but should only be carried out with experienced and knowledgeable local activity operators.

Read more: [Coastal activity adventures in Pembrokeshire](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3143)

![Three people coasteering in the sea off the coast](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__landscape__2_1x/public/media-library/2020-08/YOTS-02-1718-0010-small_0.jpg.webp?itok=82-ZRmaX)

### Carew Castle and Tidal Mill

There's a unique feel to [Castell Caeriw](https://www.visitwales.com/product/955532) (Carew Castle). Its unusual setting has something to do with it, overlooking a millpond measuring more than 23 acres. Its subsequent gentrification as a rather splendid Elizabethan country house demonstrates the rich and colourful heritage of the castle, which has recently undergone major renovation.

![Aerial view of castle with surrounding countryside and coast.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_small__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2024-07/Carew%20Castle-1%20%20Eastwood%20Photography.jpg.webp?itok=VmPrDV2F)

### Whale and dolphin watching

Harbour porpoises are easily spotted from the coast of Pembrokeshire, while there are [several boat trips](https://www.visitwales.com/search?search=boat%20trips%20Pembrokeshire&f%5B0%5D=sector%3A5002) into the deep waters nearby, where you can come across the bottlenose dolphins that live in these waters, as well as thousands of visiting dolphins in the summer months. Huge fin whales and smaller minke whales can also be seen. [Search for more boat trips in Pembrokeshire](https://www.visitwales.com/node/5427).

![Dolphins making a splash in Cardigan Bay.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2019-01/DolphinWatching_km061.jpg.webp?itok=nX3tVDqp)

Bottlenose dolphins off the Pembrokeshire coast, West Wales

### Ramsey Island RSPB reserve

[Ynys Dewi](https://www.visitwales.com/product/574808) (Ramsey Island) near Tyddewi is a natural haven featuring dramatic 120 metre high cliffs, where guillemots, razorbills, kittiwakes and fulmars nest. Peregrine falcons cruise along the cliffs, families of choughs zip in and out of the numerous caves, while the distinctive 'kronk' of the raven can also be heard.

![Boat trip off the coast of Ramsay Island](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2020-08/SVW-C19-1718-0196-small.jpg.webp?itok=kWKKCijR)

### Folly Farm

If you're looking for a fun day out for all the family, look no further than [Folly Farm](https://www.visitwales.com/node/5134)! The zoo boasts an array of animals including lions and penguins, or for a more hands-on experience there's plenty of options in the barn area. And, if that's not enough, you can experience all the fun of the fairground or let your children run wild with their imagination in the themed play areas.

![Penguins at Folly Farm.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__portrait__1_1x/public/media-library/2020-08/SVW-C03-1516-0019.jpg.webp?itok=OKTr4w53)

### The Llangwm Literary Festival

Every August, the [Llangwm Literary Festival](https://www.llangwmlitfest.co.uk/) takes place. Hosting a wide variety of workshops, thoughtful author talks, and family-friendly activities, the festival is a great place to discuss and discover all things arty.

Search for [more events in Pembrokeshire](https://www.visitwales.com/search?search=Pembrokeshire&location=&lat=51.8757077&long=-4.939193299999999&radius=80450&unit=miles&sliderValue=5&sector%5B0%5D=Event).
